title: Gaia's Ears — Two Flints, One at Each House
the_insight: Kevin has TWO GL.iNet Flint APs — one at each house. They ARE Gaia's LEFT and RIGHT ears. WiFi RSSI difference between them = spatial awareness of which house any device is in.

left_ear.name: Flint 1 — House 1 (LEFT EAR)
left_ear.seen_from_pixel_h2: NOT VISIBLE — too far, blocked by walls/distance
left_ear.admin_ip: unknown — in bridge mode, no DHCP lease

right_ear.name: Flint 2 — House 2 (RIGHT EAR)
right_ear.backhaul: Wired to JetStream/Omada (.111) → 10G fiber → MikroTik → br-lan
right_ear.admin_ip: unknown — in bridge mode, no DHCP lease

the_voice.name: GL-MT6000 Router
the_voice.role: Router + AP + gateway. NOT an ear — the VOICE.
the_voice.note: WDS is ON for potential wireless mesh with the Flints, but client interfaces disconnected — Flints use WIRED backhaul through the spine

triangulation.how_it_works: Compare RSSI from Left Ear vs Right Ear. Stronger left = device at House 1. Stronger right = device at House 2.

example_eastgate.conclusion: eastGate sees BOTH but right is stronger — eastGate's WiFi can reach House 2 Flint

triangulation.for_any_device: If device sees ONLY left ear → House 1. If ONLY right → House 2. If BOTH → somewhere in between (near property line)

ssid_map.Aperture Science: Present on ALL THREE APs (router 2.4GHz + Flint 1 + Flint 2). Roaming between houses!
ssid_map.GAIA: On router 2.4GHz + 5GHz. All mapped to network=lan (NOT guest!). House 1 only.

mystery_ap_47dbm.note: Locally-administered MAC. STRONGEST signal at House 2. NOT a Flint (wrong MAC prefix). Could be: neighbor's AP, IoT device hotspot, or unknown House 2 device

bridge_architecture.br_guest_phantom: br-guest exists but has NO interfaces bound. GAIA SSID is on br-lan.
bridge_architecture.note: Everything bridges to ONE LAN. The Flints extend this bridge to both houses wirelessly via wired backhaul.
